summary: AI observability has become a critical discipline as LLM deployments scale in complexity and cost, with the market growing to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Without proper monitoring, teams fly blind on latency spikes, prompt regressions, runaway token costs, and silent model failures that erode user experience. Gartner predicts LLM observability investments will account for 50% of GenAI deployments by 2028, up from just 15% in early 2026, underscoring the urgency for teams to adopt structured tooling now.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain execution steps, prompt inputs and outputs, latency, token usage, and evaluation scores across LangChain and non-LangChain applications
features: End-to-end run tracing with nested span visibility
Dataset management and regression testing via evaluation suites
Prompt versioning and comparison playground
Human feedback annotation and scoring workflows
Integration with LangChain, OpenAI, and custom SDKs
Team collaboration with shared projects and access controls
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces per month; Plus at $39 per seat per month with overage around $2.50 per thousand traces at standard retention; Enterprise pricing available on request
tools.best_for: Teams already using LangChain or building complex multi-step agent pipelines who need deep trace introspection and structured evaluation workflows

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token consumption, per-request cost, latency, error rates, and model usage patterns via a proxy gateway layer
features: One-line proxy setup with near-zero latency overhead
Real-time cost tracking and spend dashboards per model and user
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls
Rate limiting and budget guardrails per user or team
Prompt templating and versioning
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier
Open-source and self-hostable
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier at 10K requests per month; Pro at $79 per month with unlimited seats and usage-based overage; Team at $799 per month with compliance features; Enterprise custom pricing with SAML SSO and on-premises deployment
tools.best_for: Teams prioritising cost visibility and rapid setup who need a lightweight gateway-based monitor without complex instrumentation, especially those watching spend across multiple models

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B) Weave
tools.monitors: LLM traces, model inputs and outputs, experiment runs, evaluation metrics, dataset versions, and prompt performance across iterative development cycles
features: Trace logging with automatic capture of LLM calls and chain steps
Experiment tracking with side-by-side run comparisons
Dataset and artifact versioning integrated with model lifecycle
Built-in evaluation framework with custom and pre-built scorers
Interactive dashboards for latency, cost, and quality trends
Integrations with OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, and HuggingFace
Collaborative annotation and feedback collection
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Teams plan at $50 per user per month; Enterprise pricing on request with SSO, audit logs, and dedicated support
tools.best_for: ML research teams and data scientists who need unified experiment tracking alongside LLM observability within a single platform they may already use for traditional model training

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM span-level traces, retrieval quality in RAG pipelines, embedding drift, model performance metrics, latency, error rates, and hallucination signals at enterprise scale
features: Span-level tracing with detailed attribute capture across agents and chains
RAG retrieval evaluation including context relevance and groundedness
Experiment-style workflows for comparing prompt or model changes
Dashboards for latency, token usage, and error distribution
Online and offline evaluation with pre-built and custom metrics
OpenTelemetry-compatible instrumentation
Source-available Phoenix for self-hosting; Arize cloud for enterprise
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix open-source is free to self-host; Arize cloud platform offers a free Developer tier; Growth and Enterprise tiers priced on usage volume and seat count, available on request
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams needing production-grade LLM telemetry with strong RAG evaluation capabilities and existing ML monitoring infrastructure they want to extend to LLMs

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt versions, token usage, latency, custom evaluation scores, and user session context across self-hosted or cloud deployments
features: Detailed LLM tracing with nested observation spans
Prompt management with versioning and A/B comparison
Custom score hooks for human and automated evaluations
Dataset creation from production traces for offline testing
Cost tracking per model, user, and session
Full self-hosting option for complete data sovereignty
Strong open-source community and active development
tools.pricing: Langfuse Cloud free for under 50K requests per month; paid cloud tiers from approximately $20 per month for higher volumes; self-hosted infrastructure costs approximately $30 per month plus around 2 hours of maintenance per month
tools.best_for: Privacy-conscious teams or those in regulated industries who want full data control via self-hosting, combined with strong tracing and prompt management without vendor lock-in

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, token counts, latency, and model metadata via OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation, designed to feed into any compatible observability backend
features: OpenTelemetry-native SDK for automatic LLM call instrumentation
Support for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, HuggingFace, and other providers
Works with any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend such as Jaeger, Grafana, Datadog, or Honeycomb
Minimal code changes required for integration
Span attributes follow emerging LLM semantic conventions
Fully open-source with no vendor dependency
tools.pricing: Free and open-source; backend infrastructure costs depend entirely on the observability platform chosen to receive the telemetry data
tools.best_for: Engineering teams already invested in OpenTelemetry infrastructure who want to add LLM visibility without adopting a new proprietary platform or agent

tools.name: Confident AI (DeepEval)
tools.monitors: LLM output quality across 50+ evaluation metrics including hallucination, answer relevancy, faithfulness, toxicity, and bias, with online monitoring integrated into the observability layer
features: 50+ open-sourced evaluation metrics via the DeepEval framework
Online evaluations running automatically against live production traffic
RAG-specific metrics including contextual precision and recall
Regression testing pipelines integrated into CI/CD workflows
Evaluation-first dashboard showing quality trends over time
Used by OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft teams
Integrates DeepEval metrics directly into observability spans
tools.pricing: DeepEval open-source framework is free; Confident AI cloud platform pricing available on request with tiered plans based on evaluation volume and team size
tools.best_for: Teams where output quality and safety evaluation is the primary concern, particularly those building RAG systems or customer-facing assistants where hallucination and relevance must be continuously measured

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching aggressively: tools like Helicone offer built-in request caching so identical or near-identical prompts return stored responses without hitting the model API, which can cut costs by 20-40% for applications with repetitive query patterns such as FAQs or templated workflows

Right-size your model selection by routing requests based on complexity: use smaller, cheaper models such as GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku for simple classification or extraction tasks and reserve frontier models for tasks genuinely requiring advanced reasoning, a strategy that observability tools make measurable by exposing per-model cost and quality breakdowns

Set hard budget guardrails and rate limits per user or feature using your observability gateway: platforms like Helicone and LangSmith allow you to define spend caps that automatically throttle or alert before runaway agent loops or misconfigured prompts exhaust your monthly budget

Audit and compress your prompts regularly using trace data: observability tools expose token counts per span, making it straightforward to identify bloated system prompts or redundant context injection in RAG pipelines, where trimming unnecessary tokens can reduce per-request costs by 15-30% without degrading output quality
